Outbreak of Respiratory Illness Hits Cyprus Construction Materials Industry

NICOSIA, June 17 – A respiratory illness outbreak has affected workers at several construction materials sites in Cyprus, disrupting production and sparking concern among industry leaders, according to officials and company sources.

The Cyprus Association of Construction Materials Producers said the outbreak began last week, with more than 60 employees across multiple facilities now reported ill. Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd, one of the island’s leading cement manufacturers, confirmed that at least 18 of its staff are currently off work due to the illness. Another affected company, Limassol Aggregates, reported temporary reductions in its output as a result.

“Production lines have slowed significantly as we prioritize the health of our workers,” said Andreas Savva, operations manager at Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd. “We are working closely with health authorities to identify the source and contain the spread.”

The Ministry of Health has launched an investigation into the origin of the outbreak, which is believed to be caused by a viral agent. Symptoms reported include fever, cough and shortness of breath, but no fatalities have been linked to the illness so far.

Industry analysts warn that continued disruption could impact construction schedules across Cyprus, as several sites have reduced shifts or temporarily closed sections to sanitize facilities. “Even a short delay in cement or aggregate supply can have a cascading effect on construction projects,” said industry consultant Elena Demetriou.

The Cyprus Association of Construction Materials Producers urged companies to reinforce hygiene protocols and support affected workers. Health officials have recommended increased ventilation and use of protective equipment at sites. The situation remains under close monitoring.
